title: Is this a new usecase for old ai or has anyone done this before?
author: AccordingWarning7403
selftext:
A new teammate proposed this experiment with this use-case of AI. Take a group photo, run basic face detection on the image, extract the faces and use them in simple games. This is the first iteration of that. Their suggestion is that if we connect with library of a few more fun game mechanics this can be a fun product.  

The cool part is that since this does not involve any generative AI but strong face detection model, it's pretty fast. It gives you a game in like 2 seconds. 

Since face detection has been around for a while, it very strongly gives innovating-with-withered-technology vibe.  

What do you think? If you think this will be fun... which mechanics will be most fun for it?

comments.author: LopsidedLobster2100
comments.body: Nintendo did this with Face Raiders (3ds) and some DSi ware games did this

replies.author: AccordingWarning7403
replies.body: Good to know. We'll check it out.

comments.author: Visible-Key-1320
comments.body: I definitely would not say it's innovative, but it could be fun. The basic premise was done without face detection on the GameBoy camera in the 1990s.

replies.author: Visible-Key-1320
replies.body: I think it ultimately comes down to whether it's actually needed in the game, though. Like, it's kinda novel to shoot your friends' faces in a rail shooter, but that seems like something you pick up once, play for two minutes, and delete. But if the game actually used those faces for something interesting -- like, if your friends became your party members in an RPG, and you could choose their class and stats -- that could be a lot of fun.

replies.author: AccordingWarning7403
replies.body:
Okay... I'll suggest something on these lines to my teammate. Can create them as characters in small stories? Maybe like fables? 

Do you think a simple version of this would be fun for kids. Imagine if you could allow kids to explore stories like Gulliver's Travels or Jurasic Park where they become the characters with just a click? Or old fables like Hare and Tortoise or Greedy Farmer.

comments.author: godver3
comments.body: Seems super lame. Who would actually want to play this?

replies.author: AccordingWarning7403
replies.body: Okay. Some folks have suggested some interesting use cases. But I appreciate you sharing your thoughts.

replies.author: godver3
replies.body: I just think as presented there is nothing compelling about sticking my friend's faces onto a dull game. Maybe party games like Jackbox?

replies.author: AccordingWarning7403
replies.body: This is absolute weekend hacky proto. I understand this is not super exciting yet. Thanks for the Jackbox idea! That's soooo cool. Could set up a full memorable evening for friends. I'll keep you posted as we progress.
